title: The deeper union is not found by roaming
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: The shabad begins by naming the ordinary states the mind circles within. It then declares that the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru and crossed into by devotion and service.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person exhausted by movement, method, and spiritual curiosity that never lands. Stayed with honestly, it lets the search stop circling what is visible and return to the Guru's path.
takeaway: Roaming ends when the Guru reveals the deeper union.

lines.translation: One who loves the three qualities is subject to birth and death.
The four Vedas speak only of the visible forms.
They describe and explain the three states of mind,
but the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru. ||1||
Through devotional worship of the Lord, and service to the Guru, one swims across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਾਹੁੜਿ ਜਨਮੁ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਹੈ ਮਰਣਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: baahuR janam na hoi hai maranaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Then, one is not born again, and is not subject to death. ||1||Pause||
Everyone speaks of the four great blessings;
the Simritees, the Shaastras and the Pandits speak of them as well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਅਰਥੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ਨ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: bin gur arath beechaar na paiaa ||
lines.translation: But without the Guru, they do not understand their true significance.
The treasure of liberation is obtained through devotional worship of the Lord. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕੈ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਵਸਿਆ ਹਰਿ ਸੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kai hiradhai vasiaa har soiee ||
lines.translation: Those, within whose hearts the Lord dwells,
become Gurmukh; they receive the blessings of devotional worship.
Through devotional worship of the Lord, liberation and bliss are obtained.
Through the Guru's Teachings, supreme ecstasy is obtained. ||3||
One who meets the Guru, beholds Him, and inspires others to behold Him as well.
In the midst of hope, the Guru teaches us to live above hope and desire.
He is the Master of the meek, the Giver of peace to all.
Nanak's mind is imbued with the Lotus Feet of the Lord. ||4||12||

structure: The shabad begins by showing how much of life stays trapped inside ordinary mental states.
From there it points to a deeper union that cannot be reached by visible forms alone.
The closing movement rests with devotion and service as the actual crossing where wandering gives way.
